rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading addresses the Prophet: a mountain could not bear the Qur'an, while God steadied Muhammad to receive it, a favor to him.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون خطابا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إننا لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لما ثبت له بل انصدع من نزوله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading addresses the community: mountains would split from fear of God's warning, while humans are weaker yet more steadfast and can obey or reject amid promise and threat.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه خطاب للأمة , وأن الله لو أنذر بهذا القرآن الجبال لتصدعت من خشية الله ، والإنسان أقل قوة وأكثر ثباتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading makes the mountain a parable for disbelievers: it would humble itself at promise and split at threat, while they neither desire the promise nor fear the warning.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى ضربه مثلا للكفار أنه إذا نزل هذا القرآن على جبل خشع لوعده وتصدع لوعيده

rows.speaker: جابر بن زيد
rows.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd held that Allah is the Greatest Name because this verse names Him as Allah.
rows.anchor: كان جابر بن زيد يرى أن اسم الله الأعظم هو الله , لمكان هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the knower of the unseen and seen as knower of what is secret and public.
rows.anchor: عالم السر والعلانية , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is that God knows what was and what will be.
rows.anchor: الثاني : عالم ما كان وما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss covers what can and cannot be perceived, including life, death, lifespan, and provision.
rows.anchor: عالم ما يدرك وما لا يدرك من الحياة والموت والأجل والرزق

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl glosses this as God's knowledge of the afterlife and the present world.
rows.anchor: عالم بالآخرة والدنيا , قاله سهل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada gives al-Quddus the sense of blessed; the excerpt begins to cite Ruʾba as linguistic evidence.
rows.anchor: أنه المبارك , قاله قتادة , ومنه قول رؤبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the conquest entry into Mecca, the men pledged first and the women came afterward to pledge.
rows.anchor: لما دخل مكة عام الفتح وبايعة الرجال جاءت النساء بعدهم للبيعة فبايعهن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the Prophet sat on al-Safa with Umar below him and told Umar to take the women's pledge.
rows.anchor: أنه جلس على الصفا [ ومعه عمر أسفل منه ] فأمره أن يبايع النساء , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر عن أميمة
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir reports from Umayma that the Prophet asked her, after her own pledge, to pledge the women for him.
rows.anchor: أن تبايع النساء عنه ، قاله محمد بن المنكدر عن أميمة

rows.speaker: عامر الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the Prophet pledged the women himself with a cloth placed over his hand.
rows.anchor: أنه بايعهن بنفسه وعلى يده ثوب قد وضعه على كفه , قاله عامر الشعبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant says he placed a bowl of water, dipped his hand in it, and had the women dip theirs; this was the women's pledge.
rows.anchor: بل وضع قعبا فيه ماء وغمس فيه يده وأمرهن فغمسن أيديهن , فكانت هذه بيعة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge taught women their duties toward God and their husbands because they had entered the law without knowing its rules.
rows.anchor: كانت بيعته لهن تعريفا لهن بما عليهن من حقوق الله تعالى وحقوق أزواجهن لأنهن دخلن في الشرع ولم يعرفن حكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pledge obligation was monotheism, barring worship of anything besides God.
rows.anchor: وكان أول ما أخذه عليهن أن لا يشركن بالله شيئا توحيدا له ومنعا لعبادة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hind bint Utba was disguised, fearing the Prophet because of her treatment of Hamza and eating his liver; she said she secretly took only household provisions from Abu Sufyan and did not know whether it was lawful.
rows.anchor: أن هند بنت عتبة كانت متنكرة عند أخذ البيعة على النساء خيفة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما صنعته بحمزة وأكلها كبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the theft exchange, Abu Sufyan declared what Hind had taken, past or future, lawful; the Prophet laughed, recognized her, and she asked pardon for the past.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو سفيان : ما أصبت مما مضى أو قد بقي فهو لك حلال , فضحك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعرفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When told not to commit adultery, Hind asked the Prophet whether a free woman would commit adultery.
rows.anchor: فقالت هند يا رسول الله أو تزني الحرة ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on killing children addresses Arab practice of burying daughters alive; Hind retorted that the Prophet had killed them at Badr.
rows.anchor: لأن العرب كانت تئد البنات , فقالت هند : أنت قتلتهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil gives Hind's alternate retort: they raised the children when small, while the Muslims killed them as adults; Umar laughed until he fell back.
rows.anchor: روى مقاتل أنها قالت : ربيناهم صغارا وقتلتوهم كبارا فأنتم وهم أعلم , فضحك عمر بن الخطاب حتى استلقى

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets the invented falsehood as sorcery.
rows.anchor: أنه السحر , قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of the falsehood is gossip and striving to spread corruption.
rows.anchor: المشي بالنميمة والسعي في الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority interpret it as a wife attributing someone else's child to her husband: a foundling is what she takes between her hands, and an adulterous birth what comes between her legs.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الجمهور ألا يلحقن بأزواجهن غير أولادهن لأن الزوجة كانت تلتقط ولدا وتلحقه بزوجها ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hind said falsehood was ugly and that the Prophet commanded what was most upright and morally excellent.
rows.anchor: روي أن هندا لما سمعت ذلك قالت : والله إن البهتان لأمر قبيح , وما تأمر إلا بالأرشد ومكارم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran interprets obedience in what is right as obedience to God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: أن المعروف ها هنا الطاعة لله ولرسوله , قاله ميمون بن مهران

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب عن أم سلمة عن النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet through Shahr ibn Hawshab and Umm Salama identifies what is right as avoiding lamentation.
rows.anchor: ما رواه شهر بن حوشب عن أم سلمة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يعصينك في معروف قال : هو النوح

rows.speaker: أسيد بن أبي أسيد
rows.claim: Usayd ibn Abi Usayd says proper conduct includes not scratching the face, unbinding the hair, tearing a garment, or calling out in woe.
rows.anchor: أن من المعروف ألا تخمش وجهها ولا تنشر شعرها ولا تشق جيبا ولا تدعو ويلا ، قاله أسيد بن أبي أسيد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reads the phrase broadly as every good thing commanded by God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: أنه عام في كل معروف أمر الله ورسوله به , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hind said the women had not intended at the gathering to grant the Prophet anything; the author treats this as evidence that rulers are obeyed only in permissible good, never prohibited wrong.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن طاعة الولاة إنما تلزم في المعروف المباح دون المنكر المحظور

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the people under God's anger as the Jews.
rows.anchor: أنهم اليهود ، قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud identifies them as Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: أنهم اليهود والنصارى ، قاله ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes the people under God's anger to mean all disbelievers.
rows.anchor: جميع الكفار ، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they despaired of the afterlife's reward as disbelievers despair of the resurrection of those in graves.
rows.anchor: يئسوا من ثواب الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من بعث من في القبور ، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they despaired of reward as the dead, after seeing their fate, despaired of reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قد يئسوا من ثواب الآخرة كما يئس أصحاب القبور بعد المعاينة من ثواب الآخرة لأنهم تيقنوا العذاب ، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that they despaired of resurrection and return, as those who died and were buried despaired of it.
rows.anchor: قد يئسوا من البعث والرجعة كما يئس منها من مات منهم وقبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final reading is that they despaired of any good in the afterlife, as they despaired of good reaching them from the dead in graves.
rows.anchor: يئسوا أن يكون لهم في الآخرة خير كما يئسوا أن ينالهم من أصحاب القبور خير

none: Bare surah heading and location metadata only; no verse commentary appears in this segment.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas derives tabaraka from blessing and says it is stronger than mubarak because God alone is described by tabaraka while creatures may be mubarak.
rows.anchor: أن التبارك تفاعل من البركة , قاله ابن عباس . وهو أبلغ من المبارك لاختصاص الله بالتبارك

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata explains tabaraka as God blessing creation by placing blessing in created things.
rows.anchor: أي تبارك في الخلق بما جعل فيهم من البركة , قاله ابن عطاء

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam glosses tabaraka as exalted and elevated.
rows.anchor: معناه علا وارتفع , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the dominion in God's hand is His rule over the heavens and earth in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : ملك السموات والأرض في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq interprets the dominion as prophethood, by which God honors its followers and humiliates its opponents.
rows.anchor: ملك النبوة التي أعز بها من اتبعه وأذل بها من خالفه , قاله محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power over everything includes both granting favor and exacting vengeance.
rows.anchor: من إنعام وانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that death is in this world and life is in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يعني الموت في الدنيا , والحياة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: قتادة عن النبي
rows.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet said God humbled Adam's descendants through death, made this world a place of life then death, and the afterlife a place of recompense then permanence.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( ) إن الله أذل بني آدم بالموت , وجعل الدنيا دار حياة ثم دار موت

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil transmit another view: death and life are created as bodies, death in the form of a mottled ram and life as a spotted mare.
rows.anchor: أنه خلق الموت والحياة جسمين , فخلق الموت في صورة كبش أملح , وخلق الحياة في صورة فرس [ أنثى بلقاء ] , وهذا مأثور حكاه الكلبي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the test asks which person has the fullest intellect.
rows.anchor: أيكم أتم عقلا , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan says the test asks who is most ascetic toward worldly life.
rows.anchor: أيكم أزهد في الدنيا , قاله سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another transmitted gloss asks who most avoids God's prohibitions and hastens to obey Him.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أيكم أورع عن محارم الله وأسرع إلى طاعة الله , وهذا قول مأثور

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the best is the one who remembers death most, prepares best for it, and fears and guards against it most.
rows.anchor: أيكم للموت أكثر ذكرا وله أحسن استعدادا ومنه أشد خوفا وحذرا , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is the one who knows the defects in his own character best.
rows.anchor: أيكم أعرف بعيوب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also suggests the tested person may be the one most content with God's decree and patient under His trial.
rows.anchor: أيكم أرضى بقضائه وأصبر على بلائه

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr reads the seven heavens as matching or alike, from the sense of one thing corresponding to another.
rows.anchor: أي متفق متشابه , مأخوذ من قولهم هذا مطابق لهذا أي شبيه له , قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the seven heavens are layered one above another; the seven earths likewise lie one above another, with creation and command between each heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: يعني بعضهن فوق بعض , قال الحسن : وسبع أرضين بعضهن فوق بعض , بين كل سماء وأرض خلق وأمر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the absence of تفاوت in the Merciful's creation as absence of difference.
rows.anchor: من اختلاف , قاله قتادة , ومنه قول الشاعر :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic line uses متفاوتات as evidence for تفاوت meaning difference.
rows.anchor: متفاوتات من الأعنة قطبا حتى وفي عشية أثقالها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses تفاوت as defect.
rows.anchor: من عيب , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses تفاوت as dispersion or separation.
rows.anchor: من تفرق , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي مسلم
rows.claim: Ata ibn Abi Muslim reads it as meaning that no part falls short of another.
rows.anchor: لا يفوت بعضه بعضا , قاله عطاء بن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poem illustrates the word فات in the sense of what has escaped or been missed.
rows.anchor: فلست بمدرك ما فات مني … بلهف ولا بليت ولا لو أني

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains 'return your gaze' as looking at the sky.
rows.anchor: فارجع البصر } قال قتادة : معناه فانظر إلى السماء

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak gloss فطور as cracks.
rows.anchor: من شقوق , قاله مجاهد والضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses فطور as gaps.
rows.anchor: من خلل , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses فطور as holes.
rows.anchor: من خروق قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses فطور as weakness.
rows.anchor: من وهن , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to look twice means to inspect the sky repeatedly.
rows.anchor: أي انظر إلى السماء مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rationale for a second look is that the observer's sight is stronger and sharper the second time.
rows.anchor: لأنه في الثانية أقوى نظرا وأحد بصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another rationale is that the second look reveals the stars' movement and differing stations, confirming there is no flaw.
rows.anchor: لأنه يرى في الثانية من سير كواكبها واختلاف بروجها ما لا يراه من الأولى فيتحقق أنه لا فطور فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the two looks as an inward look of the heart and an outward look of the eye.
rows.anchor: أنه عنى بالمرتين قلبا وبصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gaze returns because it sees no cracks and so turns back.
rows.anchor: أي يرجع إليك البصر لأنه لا يرى فطورا فيرتد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses خاسئا as humbled.
rows.anchor: ذليلا , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses خاسئا as cut off.
rows.anchor: منقطعا , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam glosses خاسئا as weary or dull.
rows.anchor: كليلا , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses خاسئا as driven away, from the expression for driving away a dog.
rows.anchor: مبعدا , قاله الأخفش مأخوذ من خسأت الكلب إذا أبعدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss of حسير is regretful; an unnamed poetic line illustrates that usage.
rows.anchor: أنه النادم , ومنه قول الشاعر : ما أنا اليوم على شيء خلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says حسير is an eye exhausted and weakened in taking in what it sees; a poem illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: أنه الكليل الذي قد ضعف عن إدراك مرآه , قاله ابن عباس ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says حسير is cut off by exhaustion, citing a line about tired horses.
rows.anchor: أنه المنقطع من الإعياء , قاله السدي , ومنه قول الشاعر

none: No tafsir text is present after the bare opening brace in this segment.
No tafsir text is present after the bare opening brace in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a parable about guidance and misguidance: the face-down walker cannot see ahead or to either side, unlike an upright walker who looks around.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى للهدى والضلالة , ومعناه ليس من يمشي مكبا على وجهه ولا ينظر أمامه ولا يمينه ولا شماله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the face-down walker is the disbeliever stumbling in disbelief and the upright walker the believer guided by faith.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : أمن يمشي في الضلالة أهدى أم من يمشي مهتديا , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the face-down walker as Abu Jahl and the upright walker as Ammar ibn Yasir.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن المكب على وجهه أبو جهل بن هشام , ومن يمشي سويا عمار بن ياسر , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss of the straight path is a clear road whose traveler does not go astray; this describes the parable.
rows.anchor: أن الطريق الواضح الذي لا يضل سالكه , فيكون نعتا للمثل المضروب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the straight path is the upright truth, whose consequence is uprightness and the end of guidance.
rows.anchor: هو الحق المستقيم , قاله مجاهد , فيكون جزاء العاقبة الاستقامة وخاتمة الهداية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God scattering people in the earth as creating them there.
rows.anchor: خلقكم في الأرض , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Ibn Shajara glosses it as spreading people across the earth and dispersing them over its surface.
rows.anchor: نشركم فيها وفرقكم على ظهرها , قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also suggests that God brought people into being there until their formation is complete and their lifespan ends.
rows.anchor: أنشأكم فيها إلى تكامل خلقكم وانقضاء أجلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being gathered to God means being resurrected after death.
rows.anchor: أي تبعثون بعد الموت

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says distress appeared on the disbelievers' faces because they disliked what they witnessed.
rows.anchor: ظهرت المساءة على وجوههم كراهة لما شاهدوا , وهو معنى قول مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that evil appeared on their faces as a sign revealing their disbelief.
rows.anchor: ظهر السوء في وجهوههم ليدل على كفرهم , كقوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links faces turning white or black to the description in 3:106.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : ^ { يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه } ^ [ آل عمران : 106 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are spoken to the disbelievers by the keepers of Hell.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول خزنة جهنم لهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reads the threatened event as something they disputed and argued about.
rows.anchor: تمترون فيه وتختلفون , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says they doubted it in worldly life and claimed it would never happen.
rows.anchor: تشكون في الدنيا وتزعمون أنه لا يكون , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says they used to demand that the punishment come sooner.
rows.anchor: تستعجلون من العذاب , قاله زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba interprets the word as their invoking punishment against themselves, a derived form of دعا.
rows.anchor: أنه دعاؤهم بذلك على أنفسهم , وهو افتعال من الدعاء , قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A seventh gloss of زنيم is a man known for the trait called الأبنة; this is also reported from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: أنه الذي يعرف بالأبنة , وهو مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: أبو رزين
rows.claim: Abu Razin says زنيم is a mark of unbelief, as in the threat to mark the nose.
rows.anchor: أنه علامة الكفر كما قال تعالى : { سنسمه على الخرطوم } , قاله أبو رزين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the wealthy man with sons was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who owned a garden at Taif and had twelve sons.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه الوليد بن المغيرة , كانت له حديقة بالطائف , وكان له اثنا عشر ابنا , حكاه الضحاك

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says wealth and children are the harvest of this world, while righteous deeds are the harvest of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب : المال والبنون حرث الدنيا , والعمل الصالح حرث الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses recited to him are the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا } يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His claim that they are tales of the ancients means tales and falsehoods of earlier people.
rows.anchor: قال أساطير الأولين } يعني أحاديث الأولين وأباطيلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view is that the disbeliever receives a black mark on his nose at the resurrection, identifying him as a criminal; the author links this to 55:41.
rows.anchor: سمة سوداء تكون على أنفه يوم القيامة يتميز بها الكافر , كما قال تعالى : ^ { يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم } ^ [ الرحمن : 41 ]

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the nose will be struck in Hell on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أنه يضرب في النار على أنفه يوم القيامة , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that his name will be publicized through disgraceful deeds, so reputation rather than a physical mark brands him.
rows.anchor: أنه إشهار ذكره بالقبائح , فيصير موسوما بالذكر لا بالأثر

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says God afflicts him in this world in himself, wealth, and children with harm, humiliation, and abasement; he cites al-A'sha.
rows.anchor: هو ما يبتليه الله به في الدنيا في نفسه وماله وولده من سوء وذل وصغار , قاله ابن بحر واستشهد بقول الأعشى

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says الخرطوم means the nose for a person and the lip for an animal.
rows.anchor: الخرطوم هو من الناس الأنف , ومن البهائم الشفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read سأل سائل with hamza on both letters.
rows.anchor: قرأه الجمهور بهذين الحرفين في سأل سائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss is that someone asked when the punishment would occur, in denial.
rows.anchor: معناه استخبر مستخبر عن العذاب متى يقع , على التكذيب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says someone invoked the calamity upon them mockingly.
rows.anchor: دعا داع أن يقع البلاء بهم على وجه الاستهزاء , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third gloss takes the verb as a seeker making a request.
rows.anchor: الثالث : طلب طالب . { بعذاب واقع } وفي هذا الطالب ثلاثة أقاويل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the petitioner as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, the polytheists' standard-bearer at Badr, citing his challenge in 8:32.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد .

rows.speaker: ربيع بن أبي حمزة
rows.claim: Rabi ibn Abi Hamza says Abu Jahl was the one who said it.
rows.anchor: أنه أبو جهل : وهو القائل لذلك , قاله ربيع بن أبي حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view attributes the saying to a group of Quraysh.
rows.anchor: أنه قول جماعة من قريش

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the requested punishment is the punishment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أنه العذاب في الآخرة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed in Mecca and its punishment came at Badr through killing and capture.
rows.anchor: أنها نزلت بمكة وعذابه يوم بدر بالقتل والأسر , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: نافع وزيد بن أسلم وابنه
rows.claim: Nafi, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son read the word without hamza; they say سايل is a valley in Hell that flows with punishment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وزيد بن أسلم وابنه ( سأل سايل ) غير مهموز , وسايل واد في جهنم , وسمي بذلك لأنه يسيل بالعذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ذي المعارج as Lord of the degrees.
rows.anchor: ذي الدرجات , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses it as Lord of abundant favors and blessings.
rows.anchor: ذي الفواضل والنعم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is Lord of greatness and exaltation.
rows.anchor: ذي العظمة والعلاء

rows.speaker: قتيبة
rows.claim: Qutayba says it refers to the angels, since they ascend to God.
rows.anchor: ذي الملائكة , لأنهم كانوا يعرجون إليه , قاله قتيبة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the phrase as the stairways of heaven.
rows.anchor: أنها معارج السماء , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels and the Spirit ascend to God.
rows.anchor: إليه } أي تصعد , وفي الروح ثلاثة أقاويل

rows.speaker: قبيصة بن ذؤيب
rows.claim: Qubaysa ibn Dhu'ayb, raising it to the Prophet, says the Spirit is the soul of the deceased at the moment it is taken.
rows.anchor: أنه روح الميت حين يقبض , قاله قبيصة بن ذؤيب , يرفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the Spirit as Gabriel, as in 26:193.
rows.anchor: أنه جبريل , كما قال تعالى : ( نزل به الروح الأمين )

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says the Spirit is a created being shaped like humans but not human.
rows.anchor: أنه خلق من خلق الله كهيئة الناس وليس بالناس , قاله أبو صالح

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب والحسن
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Hasan say the day lasting fifty thousand years is the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أنه يوم القيامة , قاله محمد بن كعب والحسن

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets it as the duration of worldly life, whose elapsed and remaining years only God knows.
rows.anchor: أنها مدة الدنيا , مقدار خمسين ألف سنة , لا يدري أحد كم مضى وكم بقي إلا الله , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes it the time people would need to judge one another; God instead takes charge of their accounting much faster.
rows.anchor: أنه مقدار مدة الحساب في عرف الخلق أنه لو تولى بعضهم محاسبة بعض لكان مدة حسابهم خمسين ألف سنة

rows.speaker: معاذ عن النبي
rows.claim: Muadh reports that God accounts for them in the interval between two prayers, hence He calls Himself swiftest in reckoning.
rows.anchor: وروى معاذ عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( يحاسبهم الله بمقدار ما بين الصلاتين ولذلك سمى نفسه سريع الحساب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says beautiful patience is patience without despair or panic.
rows.anchor: أنه الصبر الذي ليس فيه جزع , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is patience without weeping or complaint.
rows.anchor: أنه الصبر الذي لا بث فيه ولا شكوى

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says it means waiting without impatience or haste.
rows.anchor: أنه الانتظار من غير استعجال , قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it means behaving graciously on the surface.
rows.anchor: أنه المجاملة في الظاهر , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet was told to endure the polytheists' accusations that he was mad, a sorcerer, and a poet.
rows.anchor: أمر بالصبر على ما قذفه المشركون من أنه مجنون وأنه ساحر وأنه شاعر , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says he was told to endure their unbelief, before fighting them was prescribed.
rows.anchor: أنه أمر بالصبر على كفرهم , وذلك قبل أن يفرض جهادهم , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event they regard as distant may be the resurrection or the punishment of the Fire.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه البعث في القيامة . الثاني : عذاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it distant may mean they think it impossible or will never occur, or that they deem the afterlife far off.
rows.anchor: مستحيل غير كائن . الثاني : استبعاد منهم للآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees it as near, meaning certain to occur, because whatever will occur is near.
rows.anchor: أي كائنا , لأن ما هو كائن قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swad ibn Qārib recounts a nocturnal caller who said a messenger from Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib had been sent to call people to God and worship; the caller repeated the message on three nights in verse.
rows.anchor: إنه قد بعث رسول من لؤي بن غالب يدعو إلى الله وإلى عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the first call Swad dismissed it and went to sleep; the next night the caller came again, stamped his foot, and repeated the summons.
rows.anchor: فقلت دعني أنام فإني أمسيت ناعسا , ولم أرفع بما قاله رأسا , فلما كان الليلة الثانية أتاني فضربني برجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the third call Swad's heart was tested by God with Islam, so he rode to Medina and found the Prophet with his companions.
rows.anchor: فلما كان الليلة الثالثة أتاني وضربني برجله , وقال قم يا سواد بن قارب فاسمع مقالتي واعقل إن كنت تعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swad asked the Prophet to hear him and recited poetry saying a messenger from Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib had come, then testified to God's oneness and Muhammad's mission.
rows.anchor: فأشهد أن الله لا شيء غيره وأنك مأمول على كل غالب . وأنك أدني المرسلين وسيلة إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and companions rejoiced at Swad's account; Umar embraced him, asked about his jinn visitor, and Swad said Quran reading had replaced that connection.
rows.anchor: ففرح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه فرحا شديدا , حتى رئي الفرح في وجوههم , قال : فوثب عمر فالتزمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swad says that after he read the Quran, his jinn visitor no longer came, and God's Book was a good replacement.
rows.anchor: [ أما ] وقد قرأت القرآن فلا , ونعم العوض كتاب الله عن الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn report that some among them are Muslims and others unjust; قاسط means one who departs from truth, illustrated by the contrast between poor and wealthy terms.
rows.anchor: وهذا إخبار عن قول الجن بحال من فيهم من مؤمن وكافر , والقاسط : الجائر , لأنه عادل عن الحق , ونظيره الترب والمترب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses القاسطون as losers.
rows.anchor: الخاسرون , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses القاسطون as sinful or wicked.
rows.anchor: الفاجرون , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses القاسطون as covenant-breakers.
rows.anchor: الناكثون , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says emphatic inna clauses in this surah quote the jinn who heard the Quran and returned to warn their people, while open anna clauses convey revelation to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ذكر ابن بحر أن كل ما في هذه السورة من ( إن ) المكسورة المثقلة فهو حكاية لقول الجن الذين استمعوا القرآن فرجعوا إلى قومهم منذرين

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب وأبو مجلز
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Abu Majliz, and others take steadfastness on the way to mean remaining in disbelief and error.
rows.anchor: أنها الإقامة على طريق الكفر والضلالة , قاله محمد بن كعب وأبو مجلز وغيرهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Qatada, and Mujahid instead take it to mean steadfastness in guidance and obedience.
rows.anchor: الاستقامة على الهدى والطاعة , قاله ابن عباس والسدي وقتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: On the disbelief reading, Muhammad ibn Ka'b says abundant water would test them by excess until they drowned, like Noah's people.
rows.anchor: بلوناهم بكثرة الماء الغدق حتى يهلكوا كما هلك قوم نوح بالغرق , وهذا قول محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation on the disbelief reading is that abundant water would grow crops and increase wealth.
rows.anchor: لأسقيناهم ماء غدق ينبت به زرعهم ويكثر مالهم

rows.speaker: السدي عن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports Umar's saying that wherever there is water there is wealth and wherever wealth is found there is temptation.
rows.anchor: حكى السدي عن عمر في قوله ( لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا ) أنه قال : حيثما كان الماء كان المال , وحيثما كان المال كانت الفتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temptation may be self-delusion or the occurrence of discord and evil because of the wealth.
rows.anchor: فاحتملت الفتنة ها هنا وجهين : أحدهما : افتننان أنفسهم . الثاني : وقوع الفتنة والشر من أجله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On the guidance reading, Ibn Abbas glosses abundant water as guidance to the straight path.
rows.anchor: معناه لهديناهم الصراط المستقيم , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the promise of abundant water means God would expand their worldly provision.
rows.anchor: لأوسعنا عليهم في الدنيا , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says it means God would give them a comfortable life.
rows.anchor: لأعطيناهم عيشا رغدا , قاله أبو العالية

rows.speaker: أبو مالك والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd interpret it as abundant wealth, a blessing that sustains life and produces fertile crops.
rows.anchor: أنه المال الواسع , لما فيه من النعم عليهم بحياة النفوس وخصب الزروع , قاله أبو مالك والضحاك وابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses غدق as fresh, accessible water.
rows.anchor: أنه العذب المعين , قاله ابن عباس
